newsitem.title: YEMEN: Saudi-funded road to be built in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-funded road to be built in Yemen.

text.p: A Yemeni contracting company on Sunday said it has been awarded a $12.2 million contract to build a new road in the impoverished state funded by Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Sultan.
"We have been awarded the contract to build a 22 km (13.7 miles) road from the southern city of Taez to Jabal Sabr," an official at Saba Trading and Contracting Co told Reuters.
Saudi Arabia's Prince Sultan, on a groundbreaking visit to Yemen in August 1996, said he would personally finance the project.

The visit, which culminated in an economic cooperation accord, came after years of strained ties over what was seen by Gulf Arab states as a sympathetic stand by Yemen towards Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
Saudi Arabia, cut off all financial aid to Yemen and expelled hundreds of thousands of Yemeni workers.
Riyadh gave Sanaa $100 million a year prior to the Gulf crisis to balance the budget in addition to financing several development projects and paying for some arms purchases.

Ties further soured when some Arab states appeared to side with a failed bid to revive the former Marxist South Yemen which merged with the north in 1990. Sanaa crushed southern troops in a two-months civil war in 1994.
Yemen and Saudi Arabia had several clashes in a potentially oil and gas-rich border area before the two sides in 1995 signed a memorandum of understanding to resolve the 60-year-old dispute.
Prince Sultan had asked a the Hael Saeed Group, one of Yemen's major contracting firms to set specifications, invite bids and award the contract on his behalf.
The road,, which will take 22 months to complete will serve tens of villages on the Jabal Sabr, a tourist attraction and home to about 90,000 Yemenis.
